It comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced an investigation into the lasting health impacts of testing exercises in the 1950s and 60s. Morris, who alongside fellow veterans have long campaigned for an investigation, said this announcement feels different "without a shadow of a doubt". "He [Burnham] has delivered something that has taken more than 70 years to come to fruition, I can't thank you enough," Morris told BBC North West Tonight . The island was a major Anglo American nuclear site in the Cold War period, lying just north of Australia. "I thought we were helping soldiers build a runway, I have no idea why, and suddenly we found out we were testing atomic bombs," Morris said. He said safety concerns when a blast went off were relaxed, with him being told to turn his back to the explosion and cover his eyes. title: The film company in Manchester that started with £50 and a camera

input.lead: Jacqui Carroll wanted to help other working class people gain experience in the industry
input.summary: Jacqui Carroll wanted to help other working class people gain experience in the industry
input.evidence_text: The film company in Manchester that started with £50 and a camera - BBC News Image caption, Jacqui Carroll wanted to give aspiring film makers new opportunities By Kelly Foran North West Published 1 hour ago In 2001, Jacqui Carroll and Terry Egan started a film and documentary company from their home with just £50, a digital video camera and a belief that everyone has a story worth telling. Now, a quarter of a century later, the stories captured on film will form part of the North West Film Archive. REELMCR was set up to help other working class people gain opportunities and experience in an industry that Jacqui said always felt like it was for a "different class". "When I was in school I said I wanted to be an actor or an astronaut and was laughed at," she said. "I was told I could be a receptionist and that's what I ended up doing. "When I was 39 and pregnant with my daughter I had to stay in and watch TV. "That's when I realised there was nobody who sounded like me and people I knew on TV. "Even in the soaps they were putting the accents on." Image caption, Terry Egan said he felt the biggest amount of pride when the people involved watched their work Jacqui and Terry decided to set up the company in Manchester making films and documentaries as well as providing training and projects in working-class communities. From the sound engineers to the scriptwriters, everyone involved was given a chance to shine. "I was a reader and got my education in other ways," said Terry, who admits he did not attend school. "But ReelMCR... it would have been just what I needed when I was growing up. "It would have made my life easier." input.summary: The prime minister vowed to get people off the streets by Christmas when he entered Downing Street
input.evidence_text: Homeless charity says 'no change' in Manchester rough sleeping despite PM's pledge - BBC News Image caption, Dave Evans co-founded a homeless charity to help support those in need By Anna Jameson and Lauren Hirst , North West Published 1 hour ago A homeless charity's co-founder has said he fears Andy Burnham will not be able to meet his pledge to end rough sleeping by Christmas as the number of those sleeping on the streets in Manchester continues to rise. The prime minister vowed to tackle the issue when he entered Downing Street in the summer, announcing a £442m package to provide emergency accommodation and practical support over three years. A further £432m was added to the scheme in October. However, with just weeks to go until Christmas, Dave Evans, from the Two Brews charity, said he believed rough sleeping had "gone up dramatically" as he witnessed the daily struggle of those on the streets. When Burnham was first elected as the Mayor of Greater Manchester in May 2017, he made the same pledge to end the need for rough sleeping across all 10 boroughs. He made a great start with the number of rough sleepers in Greater Manchester reducing during the pandemic to 89 in 2021 from 268 in 2017. But over the last five years, numbers have been creeping up. The latest annual rough sleeping snapshot, where local authorities in England provide a figure on any one night in Autumn, shows Greater Manchester has 197 rough sleepers, 43 more than in 2024. The figures for 2026 are expected early next year. 'Big increase' Jordan Parker, from Two Brews, said he and Evans had started the charity six years ago. title: Man charged with making explosives after Droylsden street evacuation

input.lead: Dozens of residents were forced to leave their homes in Droylsden for six days
input.summary: Dozens of residents were forced to leave their homes in Droylsden for six days
input.evidence_text: Man charged with making explosives after Droylsden street evacuation - BBC News Image caption, Residents were forced to leave 23 homes on Shelley Grove in the Droylsden area of Manchester By Georgie Docker North West Published 25 November 2026 A man has been charged with making explosives after dozens of residents were forced to leave their homes. People from 23 houses on Shelley Grove in Droylsden, Manchester, were evacuated on 18 November after police said a discovery had been made during an "unrelated investigation". They were only able to return six days later. James Quinn, 29, of Shelley Grove, in Droylsden, has been charged with six counts of making or possessing an explosive substance under suspicious circumstances. title: John Stones faces 2028 trial over alleged motoring offence

input.lead: The former Manchester City defender denies failing to provide driver information to police
input.summary: The former Manchester City defender denies failing to provide driver information to police
input.evidence_text: England defender John Stones faces trial in 2028 over an allegation he failed to provide driver information to police The 32-year-old footballer, who left Manchester City for Inter Milan this summer , is alleged to have driven his £150,000 Range Rover at 58mph (93km/h) in a 50mph zone on the M60 in March 2026 Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said Stones did not respond to two letters and on 27 April was charged with failing to furnish driver information. He has since pleaded not guilty Stones is represented by Freeman & Co Solicitors, a law firm whose owner Nick Freeman has advised several celebrity clients in motoring cases and has trademarked his nickname of Mr Loophole Stones now faces trial on 29 September 2028 at Warrington Magistrates' Court He has denied receiving the request for information from the police and asked prosecutors to prove it was served

In May, two hours of graft by volunteers cleared dense weeds and shrubs around the trunk of a mature tree A host of daffodils hidden underneath appeared. It was the pay-off for a bit of hard work spurred by civic pride The location is a small coppice behind Slattery family bakery and chocolatier. The wood was once the immaculate gardens of the former Whitefield Town Hall Meeting once a month, the volunteers continued to do cutting back of thick undergrowth. input.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. title: Cherki calls for more following Napoli draw

input.lead: Cherki calls for more following Napoli draw
input.summary: Rasmus Højlund grabbed the opener for the visitors after 55 minutes, latching onto Billy Gilmour’s pass before drilling into the net. Enzo Maresca’s men reacted well to the setback and levelled 12 minutes later thanks to a thunderous left-footed strike from midfield maestro Ayyou
input.evidence_text: Rasmus Højlund grabbed the opener for the visitors after 55 minutes, latching onto Billy Gilmour’s pass before drilling into the net. Enzo Maresca’s men reacted well to the setback and levelled 12 minutes later thanks to a thunderous left-footed strike from midfield maestro Ayyoub Bouaddi, who claimed his first-ever goal in senior football. With City in the ascendancy, the visitors broke on a quick counter and restored their lead through Noa Lang’s controlled volley. But Maresca’s men showed grit and determination to fight back for a second time, with UEFA’s Player of the Match Cherki precisely finding the net with four minutes of normal time left at the Etihad to earn a point. Despite another sparkling individual performance, the Frenchman made it clear that the three points are always the utmost priority. “I don’t care about scoring my goal today. I want to win, just that,” said Cherki in an honest interview after the game. “Today we played good but we didn’t put a lot of energy I think. “We need to do more. We need to win this game, today I don’t care about scoring my goal, we need to win the game. We try to put all we have on the pitch. Sometimes the game is not like how you want. “Today it’s like the last two or three games. We need to work more and come back for a win. Just that.” The draw means we have three wins, one draw and one defeat in the competition this term, with three fixtures left of the League Phase. Attention now turns to Sunday’s huge Premier League clash away to league-leaders Arsenal and Cherki explained that City only have one intention heading into London. “We are in a difficult position, that is true because we didn’t win the game,” he continued. “We’re going to London to win the game. “Nothing more.”
